description:
pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:426:

    pub struct Verifier<'a, V: SignatureVerifier, R: RevocationChecker, A: AiaFetcher = NoAiaFetcher> {

The three named trait bounds (SignatureVerifier, RevocationChecker, AiaFetcher) are exposed in the public struct declaration. Two distinct leakage modes:

1. **The bounds themselves are part of the public type signature.** A caller writing `fn my_validator<'a, V: SignatureVerifier, R: RevocationChecker, A: AiaFetcher>(v: Verifier<'a, V, R, A>) { ... }` is depending on these three trait names AND on the fact that they bound V/R/A. A future workspace refactor that splits SignatureVerifier into `RsaVerifier + EcdsaVerifier` traits, or merges RevocationChecker + AiaFetcher into a unified `NetworkOracle` trait, breaks every such caller signature.

2. **The number of generics is exposed.** Even before pattern-matching on the trait names, the fact that there are three positional generics (`Verifier<'_, V, R, A>`) is part of the spelling. Adding a 4th generic (the inevitable future trust-domain seam — pkix-ct, pkix-dane, pkix-composite, etc.) is breaking. Removing one (consolidating two seams into one) is breaking.

This is the slash-command leakage checklist's:

> Lifetime bounds, generic constraints, or associated types that expose internal data structure choices the maintainer wants to change later.

WHY IT MATTERS:

The workspace AGENTS.md commits to "three callbacks alongside SignatureVerifier (signatures) and RevocationChecker (revocation)" as the COMPLETE trust-domain seam. But the workspace also has five live adjacent-trust-domain skeleton crates (pkix-ct, pkix-dane, pkix-composite, pkix-ac) and a documented gap for future fetchers (pkix-policy-zlint subprocess fetcher, etc.). The "complete" trust-domain seam is COMPLETE-AS-CONCEIVED-2026 — and the project explicitly anticipates seam additions.

Three credible escape patterns:

(a) **Type-state Verifier with builder.** `Verifier<'_, Built>` with `VerifierBuilder<'_, State>` parameterized over a typestate sealed enum. The struct's public name doesn't carry the trait bounds; they live in the builder's signature. Adding a seam = adding a method on the builder + a typestate transition. Non-breaking.

(b) **Bundle into one trait with associated types.** `pub trait ChainBackend { type SignatureVerifier: ...; type Revocation: ...; type Aia: ...; }` and `Verifier<'_, B: ChainBackend>`. Adding an associated type to ChainBackend is technically breaking but local: only ChainBackend impl-ors care, and there are typically zero (callers use the workspace's pre-built backend struct). The verifier's surface is unchanged.

(c) **Erase to trait objects.** `Verifier<'a>` holding `&'a dyn SignatureVerifier`, `&'a dyn RevocationChecker`, `&'a dyn AiaFetcher`. Loses static dispatch on the hot signature-verify path. PKIX-sqek.4 and PKIX-sqek.20 also discuss this trade-off.

Closely related findings:

- **PKIX-sqek.19** (Verifier generics — adding a 4th seam breaks callers): same root concern, fewer specific options.
- **PKIX-sqek.4** (wrappers can't opt into AIA): wrapper-layer manifestation of the same leakage.
- **PKIX-sqek.20** (wrapper signatures locked): same shape question at the free-function layer.

The four findings (this + .4 + .19 + .20) all resolve through one shape decision; filing them separately so each angle is preserved in the bd ledger. The right resolution unifies them.

PRE-1.0 FRAMING: AGENTS.md "Project phase and decision framing" explicitly calls out trait-shape questions as architectural-completeness territory where YAGNI does NOT apply. The complete shape of the trust-domain seam should be settled before 1.0.
title: Verifier trait bounds (V: SignatureVerifier, R: RevocationChecker, A: AiaFetcher) leak the seam choice; consolidating later is breaking
